SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r6.claim: Al-Baqara’s account centers on Adam’s honor, with knowledge and vicegerency serving that theme; al-Araf has another purpose, and Adam’s honor there is secondary.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r6.anchor: القصة في هذا الموطن في كل حلقاتها ومجالاتها مبنية في الحقيقة على تكريم آدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r1.claim: After distinguishing the obedient from the disobedient, the passage recalls the first such test: angels obeyed God’s command to prostrate to Adam while Iblis refused.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r1.anchor: أخذ ينبه على أن هذا التقسيم كان في البدء الأول من أمر الله للملائكة بالسجدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r2.claim: Creation from nonexistence and formation in this remarkable shape display the Creator’s artistry; the address apparently includes all Adam’s descendants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r2.anchor: إبراز الشيء من العدم الصرف إلى الوجود والتصوير في هذه الصورة الغريبة الشكل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r3.claim: If the address is to all humanity, thumma may mean and rather than chronological sequence, or may sequence the narration rather than events; the latter is the easier reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r3.anchor: إما أن تكون فيه ثم بمعنى الواو فلم ترتب ويكون الترتيب بين الخلق والتصوير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r4.claim: Some take thumma chronologically and differ over the addressee: Adam alone, all descendants, Adam in the first clauses and descendants in the second, or Adam as an honorific plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r4.anchor: واختلفوا في المخاطب، فقيل المراد به آدم وهو من إطلاق الجمع على الواحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r5.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r5.claim: The report attributed through al-ʿAwfi says the first two clauses address Adam and the later command is narrated in sequence rather than time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r5.anchor: وروى هذا العوفي عن ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r6.claim: One report says Adam was created and formed in Paradise, then his descendants were formed in his loins at the covenant, so the sequence is chronological.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r6.anchor: خلقناكم لآدم ثم صورناكم لبنيه يعني في صلبه عند أخذ الميثاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r7.speaker: الحارث عن ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r7.claim: This account places humanity’s creation in Adam’s back and its formation in the wombs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r7.anchor: فروى الحارث عن ابن عباس خلقناكم في ظهر آدم ثم صورناكم في الأرحام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r8.speaker: ابن جبير عن ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r8.claim: This report says people were created in men’s loins and formed in women’s wombs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r8.anchor: وقال ابن جبير عنه خلقناكم في أصلاب الرجل ثم صورناكم في أرحام النساء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r9.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة والضحاك والأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r9.claim: These authorities also explain creation in men’s loins and formation in women’s wombs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r9.anchor: وقال ابن جبير عنه خلقناكم في أصلاب الرجل ثم صورناكم في أرحام النساء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r10.speaker: ابن السائب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r10.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib says people were created as drops in men’s loins and women’s chests, then formed when the drops joined in the wombs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r10.anchor: وقال ابن السائب خلقناكم نطفا في أصلاب الرجال وترائب النساء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r11.speaker: معمر بن راشد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r11.claim: Maʿmar transmits from an unnamed scholar that people were created in their mothers’ wombs and then given hearing and sight there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r11.anchor: وقال معمر بن راشد حاكيا عن بعض أهل العلم خلقناكم في بطون أمهاتكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r12.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r12.claim: A view cited from al-Qadi Abu Yaʿla supplies a deleted noun: God created people’s spirits, then formed their bodies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r12.anchor: وقيل الخطاب لبني آدم إلا أنه على حذف مضاف التقدير ولقد خلقنا أرواحكم ثم صورنا أجسامكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r13.claim: Another view supplies your father Adam and takes thumma in its ordinary chronological sense, with an interval between events.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r13.anchor: وقيل التقدير ولقد خلقنا أباكم ثم صورنا أباكم ثم قلنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r14.claim: On the turning-of-address explanation, present descendants are addressed while Adam is intended, as elsewhere Israelites are addressed about their ancestors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p15/r14.anchor: وقيل هو من تلوين الخطاب يخاطب العين ويراد به الغير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r1.claim: A tribal poem addresses descendants about their ancestors’ battle at Dhi Qar, illustrating speech directed to one generation while referring to another.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r2.claim: The clause saying Iblis was not among those who prostrated has no syntactic position and reinforces the exclusion’s denial, as the next verse’s he refused and was arrogant does.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r2.anchor: جملة لا موضع لها من الإعراب مؤكدة لمعنى ما أخرجه الاستثناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r6.claim: He links creation to God's statement that He created Adam with His hands and to the creation and shaping of humanity before commanding the angels to bow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r6.anchor: كما قال تعالى : { لما خلقت بيدي } ( ص : 75 ) وخلق أسباب تولد الفروع من الأصول

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.claim: Verses 11–27 recount Adam's creation, temptation, and expulsion from the Garden.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.anchor:
the story of Adam’s creation, temptation, and exile from
the Garden.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:9-11/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:9-11/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:9-11/r4.claim: The creation and shaping mentioned are of Adam, with the account continuing in the following verse.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:9-11/r4.anchor: يعني: آدم { ثم صورناكم } في ظهره

MAJAZ:v1p24/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p24/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p24/r8.claim: The phrase mā manaʿaka allā tasjuda means ‘what prevented you from prostrating,’ with lā extra.
MAJAZ:v1p24/r8.anchor: وفى القرآن آية أخرى: «ما منعك ألا تسجد» (7/ 11) مجازها: ما منعك أن تسجد.

ELMALILI:7:11-18/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r1.claim: God created humanity before any human individual existed, determining and bringing its first substance into being before people took their present form.
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r1.anchor: Siz hiçbir şey değil iken, siz nev‘-i beşerden hiçbir ferd âlemde mevcut değil iken, siz henüz şu bulunduğunuz şekl ü sureti ahz etmeden evvel ilk mayanızı takdir ve îcad eyledik

ELMALILI:7:11-18/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r2.claim: God then shaped people from initially formless matter, clay on earth, and a seed in their fathers’ loins into the perfected human form.
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r2.anchor: Siz ibtidâ-i hilkatte suretsiz, uzviyetsiz bir mahluk, arzda bir çamur ve babanızın sulbünde birer zerre, birer nutfe olduğunuz hâlde sizi ahsen-i takvîm olan insan suretine koyduk

ELMALILI:7:11-18/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r3.claim: The command for the angels to prostrate to Adam means that they should serve him with submission, obedience, and compliance.
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r3.anchor: Ona boyun eğip itaat ve inkıyâd ile hizmet eyleyin

ELMALILI:7:11-18/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r4.claim: The plural address to humanity concerns the human race as a whole, and the prostration of the angels to Adam is recalled as a favor to humankind.
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r4.anchor: Bu hitapların bir ferde veya sınıfa değil, ale’l-umûm cins-i beşere

ELMALILI:7:11-18/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r5.claim: The command to prostrate honors the whole human species, including Adam’s descendants, rather than Adam alone.
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r5.anchor: bu secde emri Hazret-i Âdem’in şahsına mahsus değil, zürriyeti de dâhil olmak üzere nev‘ine ait bir şeref ve imtiyazdır

ELMALILI:7:11-18/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r6.claim: Adam’s descendants include eminent prophets of great resolve who are superior to Adam himself, supporting the species-wide meaning of the honor.
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r6.anchor: Zürriyet-i Âdem içinde bizzat Hazret-i Âdem’den efdal olan ulü’l-azm enbiyâ-yı izâm gibi zevât bulunduğu şüphesiz

ELMALILI:7:11-18/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r7.claim: The discourse is better read by treating Adam as a universal exemplar representing human nature and the whole human species, not merely as the first individual.
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r7.anchor: ale’l-umûm nev‘-i beşerin mâhiyetini temsil eden bir misâl-i kül

ELMALILI:7:11-18/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r8.claim: As father of humanity, Adam potentially possessed the virtues and faculties that would appear in all his descendants; thus his creation, shaping, and the angels’ prostration encompass all humanity.
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r8.anchor: bütün zürriyetinde tecellî edecek olan fezâil ü melekâtı da bilkuvve hâiz olmak itibariyle ebü’l-beşer olarak teemmül edildiği zamandır ki hilkat-i Âdem hilkat-i benî Âdem’i, tasvîr-i Âdem tasvîr-i benî Âdem’i, Âdem’e secde bütün nev‘-i beşere secdeyi mutazammın olduğu tevazzuh eder

ELMALILI:7:11-18/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r9.claim: This passage clarifies the meaning of humanity’s appointment as successors on earth in al-An‘am.
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r9.anchor: mânasını da tavzih eden bu âyetin mazmûnu

ELMALILI:7:11-18/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r10.claim: God bestowed such honor on humanity that He commanded angels to prostrate to Adam, and worshipping other than God after these gifts is profound abasement, ingratitude, and a cause of grave responsibility.
ELMALILI:7:11-18/r10.anchor: Âdem’in melâikeye değil, melâikenin Âdem’e secde etmesini emretmiştir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.claim: The Adam–Satan episode explains the history of hostility between Satan and Adam's descendants and points to its cause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.anchor: It shows the history of the enmity between Adam and his progeny with Satan and his accomplices.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.claim: Khalaqa means to design; used alone it includes creation's consequences and connections, while accompanying terms narrow it to its literal meaning.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.claim: Here ‘creating’ and ‘giving form’ denote creation's initial design and its final form and perfection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.anchor: The initial phase of every creation is its design ad its final phase is the form and perfection given to it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.claim: The address is to Quraysh, who are being reminded of human creation's phases and the trials ordained for them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.anchor: Here the addressees, as indicated earlier, are the Quraysh. They are being informed of the about the phases of creation of human beings and of the trials ordained for them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.claim: Adam's story belongs to humanity as a whole because he is the father of humankind.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.anchor: Adam (sws) is the father of all humankind. Hence his anecdote is not solely his; it is that of the whole humankind.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.claim: Iblis is the title of the jinn who deceived Adam and rebelled against God by disobeying Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.anchor: who had deceived Adam (sws). He was from among the jinn and had become rebellious by disobeying God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.claim: Human and jinn followers of Iblis are treated as his progeny and are called Satans in the Qur'an; Satan is not an independent creation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.anchor: It for such humans and jinn that the Qur’ān uses the word “Satan.” It is not an independent creation, as has been explained in Sūrah al-Baqarah.

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r1.claim: This passage is the second account in the Quran’s textual order of Adam’s creation, temptation, and banishment; related accounts occur elsewhere.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r1.anchor: The narrative in these verses represents the second account (in the textual order of the Quran) of Adam’s creation, temptation, and banishment;

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r2.claim: The plural address includes all humanity, originally created with Adam as the seed in his loins, so humanity shares the story, Adam’s honor, and its commands and warnings.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r2.anchor: all human beings can be understood as having participated in the events of the narrative that follows

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r3.claim: The shared primordial human story is connected with the pretemporal covenant in which all humanity witnessed to God’s Lordship.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r3.anchor: where all human beings bear witness to God’s Lordship in a pretemporal covenant:

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r4.speaker: Ṭ, Th
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r4.claim: The verse is read as mankind’s creation as a whole through Adam, followed by God’s shaping each individual in the womb or in Adam’s loins.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r4.anchor: then We formed you refers to God’s shaping each individual, in either the womb of the mother or the loins of Adam (Ṭ, Th).

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r5.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r5.claim: Another reading takes creation and formation to refer directly to Adam and only representatively to the rest of humanity.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r5.anchor: Others considered these statements to refer directly to God’s creation and formation of Adam

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r6.claim: The Quran also describes God creating the first human from clay with His two Hands.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r6.anchor: For God’s having created the first human being from clay with His two Hands, see 38:71–75.

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r7.claim: The command that angels prostrate to Adam recurs in the Adam accounts and can imply that primordial humanity stood above the angels.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r7.anchor: is a key element in all accounts of Adam’s creation (2:34; 15:29; 17:61; 18:50; 20:116; 38:73–74)

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r8.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r8.claim: Some commentators treat the prostration as symbolic, or say the angels bowed to God with Adam as their prayer direction.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r8.anchor: they say that the angels were ultimately bowing to God and taking Adam as their qiblah, or direction of prayer (R).

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r9.claim: Prostration can honor another’s spiritual greatness without worship, as in Joseph’s family bowing to him.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r9.anchor: It is also possible to prostrate in recognition of the spiritual greatness of another rather than as a form of worship;

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r10.claim: The wording makes Iblis seem to belong to the angels, supporting that classification, while 18:50 calls him one of the jinn; scholars debate the issue.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r10.anchor: suggests that Iblīs is among the angels, represents an important Quranic basis for the idea that Iblīs was himself an angel

TABATABAI:7:16-17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:16-17/r6.speaker: الأخفش
TABATABAI:7:16-17/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash reads ثم in 'We created you, then fashioned you' as meaning و.
TABATABAI:7:16-17/r6.anchor: قال الأخفش { ثم } هيهنا في معنى الواو

TABATABAI:7:16-17/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:16-17/r7.speaker: الزجاج
TABATABAI:7:16-17/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects that reading because ثم marks what occurs later; he interprets the sequence as Adam's creation from earth, his later fashioning, and then the command to prostrate.
TABATABAI:7:16-17/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج وهذا خطأ لا يجوزه الخليل وسيبويه وجميع من يوثق بعلمه

TABATABAI:7:16-17/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:16-17/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABATABAI:7:16-17/r8.claim: This sequential account of creating and fashioning Adam before commanding prostration is also reported from al-Hasan.

TABATABAI:7:16-17/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:16-17/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:16-17/r9.claim: Arabic may attribute an act to descendants while referring to their ancestors, as in the covenant and the raising of the mountain.
TABATABAI:7:16-17/r9.anchor: ومن كلام العرب فعلنا بكم كذا وكذا وهم يعنون أسلافهم

TABATABAI:7:10-25/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الربيع، قتادة، السدي
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Rabi', Qatada, and al-Suddi say humanity was created when Adam was made and then fashioned in his loins.
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والربيع وقتادة والسدي

TABATABAI:7:10-25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r2.speaker: جماعة من النحويين
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r2.claim: A group of grammarians, including Ali ibn Isa and Qadi Abu Sa'id al-Sirafi, say the order is only in the telling, not the chronology.
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r2.anchor: وهذا قول جماعة من النحويين منهم علي بن عيسى والقاضي أبو سعيد السيرافي وغيرهما

TABATABAI:7:10-25/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r3.claim: On the narration-order reading, Ikrima says people were created in men's loins and fashioned in women's wombs.
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة وقيل خلقناكم في الرحم ثم صورناكم بشق السمع والبصر وسائر الأعضاء

TABATABAI:7:10-25/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r4.claim: Another account says people are created in the womb and then fashioned by the formation of hearing, sight, and the other organs.
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r4.anchor: وقيل خلقناكم في الرحم ثم صورناكم بشق السمع والبصر وسائر الأعضاء

TABATABAI:7:10-25/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r5.claim: Attributing an ancestor's quality or act to descendants requires shared participation in that kind of act, not mere kinship; Adam's creation cannot simply be called their creation.
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r5.anchor: إن نسبة شيء من صفات السابقين أو أعمالهم إلى أعقابهم إنما تصح إذا اشترك القبيلان في ذلك بنوع من الاشتراك كما فيما أورده من المثال لا بمجرد علاقة النسب

TABATABAI:7:10-25/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r6.claim: If Adam's creation counted as his descendants' creation, prostration to Adam should likewise count as prostration to them, yet the verse specifically names Adam.
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r6.anchor: وثانيا أن ما ذكره لو صح به أن يعد خلق آدم وتصويره خلقا وتصويرا لبنيه

TABATABAI:7:10-25/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r7.claim: The other proposed interpretations are implausible and do not follow from the verse's wording.
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r7.anchor: وأما ما نقله أخيرا من أقوالهم فوجوه سخيفة غير مفهومة من لفظ الآية

TABATABAI:7:10-25/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r8.claim: All the angels prostrated, as the explicit wording in al-Hijr confirms, while Iblis alone was excluded.
TABATABAI:7:10-25/r8.anchor: أخبر تعالى عن سجود الملائكة جميعا كما يصرح به في قوله فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r1.claim: The description of the angels as honored servants who act by God's command indicates that Iblis was not of their kind.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r1.anchor: وهو بظاهره يدل على أنه من غير نوع الملائكة

TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r2.speaker: القائلون بالاستثناء المتصل
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r2.claim: One view treats Iblis as a connected exception by subsuming him under the angels, who were more numerous and superior.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r2.anchor: وقع الخلاف بينهم في توجيه هذا الاستثناء أهو استثناء متصل بتغليب الملائكة لكونهم أكثر وأشرف

TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r3.speaker: القائلون بالاستثناء المنفصل
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r3.claim: Another view treats Iblis as a disconnected exception who received a separate command from the one addressed to the angels.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r3.anchor: أو أنه استثناء منفصل وإنما أمر بأمر على حدة غير الأمر المتوجه إلى جميع الملائكة

TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r4.claim: The phrase asking what prevented Iblis from prostrating when commanded suggests there was only one command, directed to the angels.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r4.anchor: أن الأمر لم يكن إلا واحدا وهو الذي وجهه الله إلى الملائكة

TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r5.claim: The apparent Qur'anic account places Iblis among the angels without distinguishing him, in the holy station associated with the vicegerency story.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#2/r5.anchor: والذي يستفاد من ظاهر كلامه تعالى أن إبليس كان مع الملائكة من غير تميز له منهم والمقام الذي كان يجمعهم جميعا كان هو مقام القدس

TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r1.claim: The prostration command addresses the station and those dwelling there; the command to descend from it shows that the pronoun refers to a rank, sky, or garden, all understood as a station.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r1.anchor: وأن الأمر بالسجود إنما كان متوجها إلى ذلك المقام أعني إلى المقيمين بذلك المقام من جهة مقامهم

TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r2.claim: After the human creation, the angels remain in obedient submission while Iblis leaves their station; fisq means a fruit's exit from its husk, and his existence becomes departure from divine honor and servitude.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r2.anchor: والفسق خروج التمرة عن قشرها فتميز منهم فأخذ حياة لا حقيقة لها إلا الخروج من الكرامة الإلهية وطاعة العبودية

TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r3.claim: Though told in familiar social terms of command, obedience, rebellion, and expulsion, the story represents creation: Iblis refused submission to human reality, and arrogance made him fall from a station that cannot admit it.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r3.anchor: غير أن البيان السابق على استفادته من الآيات يهدينا إلى كونها تمثيلا للتكوين بمعنى أن إبليس على ما كان عليه من الحال لم يقبل الامتثال أي الخضوع للحقيقة الإنسانية

TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r4.claim: The same command addressed both angels and Iblis; the angels' command is not a legislative test because they are naturally obedient, while Iblis belongs to the opposing side.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r4.anchor: أمر واحد توجه إلى الملائكة وإبليس جميعا بعينه

TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r5.claim: Without Adam's creation and the command to prostrate, Iblis would have remained indistinguishable from the angels; humanity split the station into closeness and distance, and the paths of felicity and misery.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#3/r5.anchor: فلولا أن الله سبحانه خلق آدم وأمر الملائكة وإبليس جميعا بالسجود له لكان ابليس على ما كان عليه من منزلة القرب غير متميز من الملائكة

TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r1.claim: The bowing honored Adam for being formed and receiving God’s spirit, not for his earthly material; merit in created things follows divine care rather than their substance.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r1.anchor: لمادته الأرضية التي سوي منها، وإنما دعوا إلى ذلك لما سواه ونفخ فيه من روحه الخاص به تعالى الحاملة للشرف كل الشرف

TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r1.claim: Iblis sinned and deserved expulsion by arrogantly refusing God’s command; his words express pride against God, while the verses focus on that rebellion.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r1.anchor: أن إبليس إنما عصى واستحق الرجم بالتكبر على الله في عدم امتثال أمره

TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r1.claim: The prostration story depicts real relations among humanity, angels, and Iblis through the narrative of command, obedience, pride, expulsion, and dialogue; objections arise from neglecting its meaning.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r1.anchor: وجدتها صورة منبئة عن الروابط الواقعية التي بين النوع الإنساني والملائكة وإبليس

TABATABAI:7:10-25#31/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#31/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#31/r4.claim: The assertion that scholars unanimously held jinn and angels to be subtle airy bodies that physically change forms has no sound transmitted or rational proof; claimed consensus is not authoritative.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#31/r4.anchor: لا دليل عليه من نقل ثابت أو عقل، وأما ما ادعي من الإجماع ومآله إلى الاتفاق في الفهم فلا حجية لمحصله

TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r7.claim: Al-Sadiq says Iblis was never an angel or a manager of heaven, though the angels thought he belonged to them and God knew otherwise.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r7.anchor: فقال لم يكن من الملائكة وكانت الملائكة ترى أنه منها

TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r8.speaker: الطيار
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r8.claim: Al-Tayyar objects that Iblis must have been an angel because God included him in the command to the angels to bow to Adam.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r8.anchor: فأتيت الطيار فأخبرته بما سمعت فأنكر وقال كيف لا يكون من الملائكة؟ والله يقول للملائكة

TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r9.claim: Al-Sadiq answers that the address “O you who believe” can include hypocrites and the misguided, so an inclusive address does not prove Iblis was an angel.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r9.anchor: قال له قول الله عز وجل { يا أيها الذين آمنوا } في غير مكان في مخاطبة المؤمنين

TAB-FULL:v10p75/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says خلقناكم refers to Adam, while صورناكم refers to Adam’s descendants.
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولقد خلقناكم ثم صورناكم} [الأعراف: 11]

TAB-FULL:v10p75/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r2.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says God created Adam and then shaped the descendants in their mothers’ wombs.
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r2.anchor: عن الربيع: {ولقد خلقناكم} [الأعراف: 11] يعني: " آدم، {ثم صورناكم} [الأعراف: 11] يعني: «في الأرحام»

TAB-FULL:v10p75/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says God created Adam and then shaped his descendants in the wombs.
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r3.anchor: عن السدي: {ولقد خلقناكم ثم صورناكم} [الأعراف: 11] يقول: «خلقنا آدم ثم صورنا الذرية في الأرحام»

TAB-FULL:v10p75/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r4.claim: Qatada says Adam was created from clay and people were then formed in the womb through successive stages: clot, lump, bones, flesh, and a new creation.

TAB-FULL:v10p75/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r5.claim: In another report, Qatada says God created Adam and then formed his descendants after him.
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r5.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة، قال: «خلق الله آدم ثم صور ذريته من بعده»

TAB-FULL:v10p75/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the people shaped as Adam’s descendants, after saying that Adam is the one created.

TAB-FULL:v10p75/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r7.claim: Another view takes the creation as occurring in fathers’ loins and the shaping as occurring in mothers’ wombs.
TAB-FULL:v10p75/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: ولقد خلقناكم في أصلاب آبائكم ثم صورناكم في بطون أمهاتكم

TAB-FULL:v10p78/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r1.claim: Ikrima says people were created in men’s loins and shaped in women’s wombs.
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة: {ولقد خلقناكم ثم صورناكم} [الأعراف: 11] قال: «خلقناكم في أصلاب الرجال، وصورناكم في أرحام النساء»

TAB-FULL:v10p78/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r2.speaker: الأعمش
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads the verse with an explanatory gloss that creation is in men’s loins and shaping in women’s wombs.
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r2.anchor: سمعت الأعمش، يقرأ: {ولقد خلقناكم ثم صورناكم} [الأعراف: 11] قال: «خلقناكم في أصلاب الرجال، ثم صورناكم في أرحام النساء»

TAB-FULL:v10p78/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r3.claim: Mujahid says God created Adam and shaped the descendants in Adam’s back.
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {ولقد خلقناكم} [الأعراف: 11] قال:

TAB-FULL:v10p78/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r4.claim: In one report, Mujahid says the descendants were in Adam’s back as those who would later receive their reward in the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r4.anchor: سمعت مجاهدا في قوله: {ولقد خلقناكم ثم صورناكم} [الأعراف: 11] قال: «في ظهر آدم لما تصيرون إليه من الثواب في الآخرة»

TAB-FULL:v10p78/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r5.claim: Another view says people were created in their mothers’ wombs and shaped there.
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك: ولقد خلقناكم في بطون أمهاتكم، ثم صورناكم فيها

TAB-FULL:v10p78/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r6.speaker: عمن ذكره
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r6.claim: An unnamed authority cited through Maʿmar says God creates a person in the womb and then shapes him, opening his hearing, sight, and fingers.
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r6.anchor: عن معمر، عمن ذكره قال: {خلقناكم ثم صورناكم} [الأعراف: 11] قال: «خلق الله الإنسان في الرحم، ثم صوره فشق سمعه وبصره وأصابعه»

TAB-FULL:v10p78/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r7.claim: Tabari prefers that God created Adam and shaped the descendants through shaping Adam, whose action is attributed to them.
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r7.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وأولى الأقوال بالصواب قول من قال: تأويله: {ولقد خلقناكم} [الأعراف: 11]

TAB-FULL:v10p78/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r8.claim: Tabari compares this address to 2:63, where God addresses Jews present in the Prophet’s time about the covenant and the Mount, though the acts belonged to their forebears.
TAB-FULL:v10p78/r8.anchor: وكما قال جل ثناؤه لمن بين أظهر المؤمنين من اليهود على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v10p80/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r1.claim: Tabari argues that ثم signals that what follows occurs after what precedes; the command to prostrate therefore followed Adam’s creation and shaping, before his descendants were shaped in wombs.
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r1.anchor: و (ثم) في كلام العرب لا تأتي إلا بإيذان انقطاع ما بعدها عما قبلها

TAB-FULL:v10p80/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r2.claim: A poetic use of ثم for واو is a metrical necessity and cannot control the Qur’anic reading, which has a clear, established sense in eloquent Arabic.
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r2.anchor: سألت ربيعة من خيرها … أبا ثم أما فقالت لمه

TAB-FULL:v10p80/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r3.claim: Tabari rejects the claim that the order is reversed, with creation followed by the command and then shaping; Arabs do not put ثم before what it is meant to precede without contextual evidence.
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r3.anchor: لا تدخل (ثم) في الكلام وهي مراد بها التقديم على ما قبلها من الخبر

TAB-FULL:v10p80/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r4.claim: After shaping Adam into a complete form and breathing into him of His spirit, God commanded the angels to prostrate as a test distinguishing the obedient from the disobedient; they prostrated except Iblis.
TAB-FULL:v10p80/r4.anchor: فلما صورنا آدم وجعلناه خلقا سويا، ونفخنا فيه من روحنا، قلنا للملائكة: اسجدوا لآدم، ابتلاء منا واختبارا لهم بالأمر

TABATABAI:7:10-11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r4.claim: The creation and prostration account begins here and extends fifteen verses, expanding the previous verse’s summary and explaining how humanity came to be established on earth; the oath-like lām marks its opening.
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r4.anchor: صورة قصة تبتدئ من هذه الآية إلى تمام خمس عشرة آية يفصل فيها إجمال الآية السابقة

TABATABAI:7:10-11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r5.claim: The prostration and Garden episodes are presented as one connected story, ending with the decree of descent and earthly settlement, so the detailed story matches 7:10’s summary.
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r5.anchor: سيقت القصتان أعني قصة الأمر بالسجدة

TABATABAI:7:10-11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r6.claim: The address “We created you then fashioned you” is to all humanity and is an address of blessing, as in the preceding verse; it restates the same substance in fuller detail.
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r6.anchor: الخطاب فيه لعامة الآدميين وهو خطاب امتناني كما مر نظيره في الآية السابقة

TABATABAI:7:10-11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r7.claim: The angels’ prostration was for all human descendants, with Adam as the appointed direction and representative of humanity, not the object because of his individual person; the Kaaba similarly directs worship toward lordship.
TABATABAI:7:10-11/r7.anchor: السجدة كانت من الملائكة لجميع بني آدم أي للنشأة الإنسانية وإن كان آدم عليه السلام هو القبلة المنصوبة للسجدة

TABATABAI:7:18-20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r1.claim: The satanic influence on human beings reaches their consciousness and practical thought: their representations of things and judgments about what should or should not be done.
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r1.anchor: والثانية أن الذي يمسه الشيطان من بني آدم

TABRISI:7:10-11/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:10-11/r12.claim: Khalq is bringing a thing into existence according to wisdom’s measure; taṣwīr is giving it a form whose structure defines its outward configuration.
TABRISI:7:10-11/r12.anchor: والخلق إحداث الشيء على تقدير تقتضيه الحكمة والتصوير جعل الشيء على صورة من الصور

TABRISI:7:10-11/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:10-11/r13.claim: Sujūd fundamentally means lowering oneself, and properly refers to placing the forehead on the ground.
TABRISI:7:10-11/r13.anchor: والسجود أصله الانخفاض وحقيقته وضع الجبهة على الأرض

TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r5.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash takes thumma here to mean wāw, coordinating creation and shaping without chronological sequence.
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r5.anchor: قال الأخفش: ثم ها هنا في معنى الواو

TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj rejects al-Akhfash’s reading: Khalīl, Sībawayh, and trusted grammarians do not allow thumma to mean wāw; it marks what follows in time.
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: وهذا خطأ لا يجيزه الخليل وسيبويه وجميع من يوثق بعلمه إنما ثم للشيء الذي يكون بعد المذكور قبله

TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r7.claim: The sequential account concerns Adam: God created him from earth, then formed him, then commanded the angels after completing his creation; this sequence is reported from al-Hasan.
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r7.anchor: بعد الفراغ من خلق آدم فثم إنما هو لما بعد وهذا مروي عن الحسن

TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r8.claim: The plural address can refer to ancestors, as in the Qur’anic reminder that God took your covenant and raised the mountain over you, meaning your ancestors’ covenant.
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r8.anchor: ومن كلام العرب فعلنا بكم كذا وكذا وهم يعنون أسلافهم وفي التنزيل وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور

TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والربيع وقتادة والسدي
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Rabiʿ, Qatada, and al-Suddi say God created Adam, then formed you in his back, then commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam.
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r9.anchor: أن معناه خلقنا آدم ثم صورناكم في ظهره ثم قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والربيع وقتادة والسدي

TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r10.speaker: علي بن عيسى والقاضي أبو سعيد السيرافي
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r10.claim: A group of grammarians, including Ali ibn Isa and Qadi Abu Saʿid al-Sirafi, says the sequence is in the order of narration: then We tell you that We commanded the angels.
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r10.anchor: وهذا قول جماعة من النحويين منهم علي بن عيسى والقاضي أبو سعيد السيرافي وغيرهما

TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r11.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r11.claim: On the narration-order explanation, Ikrima says God created people in men’s loins and formed them in women’s wombs.
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r11.anchor: خلقناكم في أصلاب الرجال ثم صورناكم في أرحام النساء عن عكرمة

TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r12.speaker: يمان
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r12.claim: Yaman says people are created in the womb and then formed through the opening of hearing, sight, and the other bodily members.
TABRISI:7:10-11#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: خلقناكم في الرحم ثم صورناكم بشق السمع والبصر وسائر الأعضاء عن يمان

TABRISI:7:10-11#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:10-11#3/r1.claim: A poet’s answer that names father before mother illustrates ordering in speech: first answer about the father, then the mother.
TABRISI:7:10-11#3/r1.anchor: فمعناه لتجيب أولا عن الأب ثم الأم

TABRISI:7:10-11#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:10-11#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:10-11#3/r2.claim: The commentary on the angels’ prostration and Iblis’s exception has already been given in the discussion of this passage in Surat al-Baqara.
TABRISI:7:10-11#3/r2.anchor: قد مضى الكلام فيه في سورة البقرة

THALABI:v4p217#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p217#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p217#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God created your origin and father Adam, then formed you in your mothers’ wombs.
THALABI:v4p217#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: خلقنا أصلكم وأباكم آدم ثم صورناكم في أرحام أمهاتكم

THALABI:v4p217#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p217#2/r2.speaker: قتادة والربيع والضحاك والسدي
THALABI:v4p217#2/r2.claim: Qatada, al-Rabiʿ, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi say the creation was Adam, while the shaping was his descendants.
THALABI:v4p217#2/r2.anchor: قال قتادة والربيع والضحاك والسدي: أما خلقناكم فآدم وأما صورناكم فذريته

THALABI:v4p217#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p217#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p217#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says God created Adam and then shaped his descendants in Adam’s back.
THALABI:v4p217#2/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: خلقنا آدم ثم صورناكم في ظهر آدم

THALABI:v4p217#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p217#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v4p217#2/r4.claim: Ikrima says humans were created in men’s loins and shaped in women’s wombs.
THALABI:v4p217#2/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: خلقناكم في أصلاب الرجال وصورناكم في أرحام النساء

THALABI:v4p217#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p217#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v4p217#2/r5.claim: Ata says humans were created in Adam’s back and then shaped in wombs.
THALABI:v4p217#2/r5.anchor: قال عطاء: خلقوا في ظهر آدم ثم صوروا في الأرحام

THALABI:v4p217#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p217#2/r6.speaker: يمان
THALABI:v4p217#2/r6.claim: Yaman says the human is created in the womb and shaped as hearing, sight, and fingers are opened and formed.
THALABI:v4p217#2/r6.anchor: وقال يمان: خلق الإنسان في الرحم ثم صوره ففتق سمعه وبصره وأصابعه

THALABI:v4p217#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p217#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p217#2/r7.claim: The author raises the sequencing problem: ثم normally implies order and delay, although the angelic command to prostrate precedes human creation and shaping.
THALABI:v4p217#2/r7.anchor: فإن قيل: ما وجه قوله ثم قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم وإنما خلقنا بعد ذلك وثم يوجب الترتيب والتراخي

THALABI:v4p217#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p217#2/r8.speaker: قوم
THALABI:v4p217#2/r8.claim: Some say the wording uses fronting and postponement.
THALABI:v4p217#2/r8.anchor: قلنا: قال قوم: على التقديم والتأخير

THALABI:v4p217#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p217#2/r9.speaker: يونس
THALABI:v4p217#2/r9.claim: Yunus says creation and shaping are one act; the plural address may refer to the whole group through its leader, as saying you were beaten when only its chief was struck.
THALABI:v4p217#2/r9.anchor: قال يونس: الخلق والتصوير واحد [ ... ] إلينا، كما نقول: قد ضربناكم وإنما ضربت سيدهم

THALABI:v4p217#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p217#2/r10.speaker: الأخفش
THALABI:v4p217#2/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash takes ثم as meaning و, supported by a poetic line that says a person asked about her best “father then mother” to mean father and mother.
THALABI:v4p217#2/r10.anchor: قال الأخفش: ثم بمعنى الواو ومجازه: قلنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas takes 'We created you' to mean Adam, and 'then shaped you' to mean his descendants.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r2.claim: Mujahid likewise says Adam was created and his descendants were shaped in Adam's back.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r3.claim: The plural 'We created you' can refer to Adam because he is the father of humankind and his creation included descendants who would emerge from his loins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r3.anchor: لأنه أبو البشر وفي خلقه خلق يخرج من صلبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r4.speaker: يونس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r4.claim: Yunus says 'then We shaped you' may refer to Adam alone, just as a plural expression can refer to a people's chief.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r4.anchor: وهو قول يونس (¬7)، قال: (يجوز أن يكون معنى {صورناكم} لآدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r5.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers Mujahid's interpretation, citing what follows in the verse; the excerpt ends before his evidence is given.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38/r5.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد (¬10) في هذه الآية قول مجاهد لقوله بعده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r1.claim: The command to prostrate came after Adam and his descendants were created and shaped, as the sequence marked by ثم indicates.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r1.anchor: وكان قوله: {للملائكة اسجدوا} قبل خلق ذرية آدم وتصويرهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r2.claim: Taking creation and shaping as referring to Adam's descendants in the wombs fails to observe the ordering imposed by ثم.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r2.anchor: فمن جعل الخلق والتصوير في هذه الآية لأولاد آدم في الأرحام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r3.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash allows ثم here to mean واو, which removes the implication of delayed sequence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r3.anchor: إلا أن يأخذ. بقول الأخفش فإنه يقول: ((ثم) هاهنا في معنى الواو)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects al-Akhfash's interpretation of ثم as واو, invoking the authority of al-Khalil, Sibawayh, and trusted grammarians.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: (وهذا خطأ لا يجيزه الخليل (¬3) وسيبويه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says God created Adam and shaped his descendants in his back, then ordered the prostration.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيد (¬6): (وقد بينه مجاهد (¬7) حين قال: إن الله خلق آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r6.claim: The passage says another report makes the sequence clear: God brought Adam's descendants out from his back in the primordial covenant episode.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r6.anchor: وهذا بين في حديث [آخر] (¬9) وهو أنه أخرجهم من ظهر آدم في سورة الذر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r7.claim: The exception is not from the angels as a group but from those ordered to prostrate alongside them; 7:12 confirms Iblis was ordered.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p38#2/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج: (وهو استثناء ليس من الأول ولكنه ممن أمر بالسجود مع الملائكة

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r1.claim: Khalq means creating and bringing into existence from nonexistence; taswir means giving something form and shape.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r1.anchor: Sözlükte halk, “yaratma, yokluktan varlık alanına çıkarma”, tasvîr ise “bir şeye sûret ve şekil verme” demektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r2.claim: Khalq can denote creation without form and taswir the ordering of chaos into cosmos; the relation between the terms and thumma, which marks sequence as well as rank and development, suggests human development from embryo toward physical and spiritual maturity and the species’ bodily and intellectual development.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r2.anchor: bu iki kavramın anlam ilişkisi ve onların “sümme” edatıyla birbirine bağlanması, bu edatın ise olaylar arasındaki zaman (öncelik-sonralık) ilişkisi yanında mertebe

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r3.claim: The continuation of the verse makes the collective development of the human species from its first creation the stronger reading.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r3.anchor: Âyetin devamından bu son anlamın daha ağırlıklı olduğu anlaşılmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r4.claim: Existence and becoming human are themselves gifts, so the verse reminds polytheists and humanity to recognize God the benefactor and worship Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r4.anchor: Yok iken var olmak gibi insan ve insanlık hüviyetini kazanmak da bizâtihi hayır ve lutuf olduğu için insanlığın ulaştığı bu mazhariyet bilhassa müşriklere

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r5.claim: Although Adam’s creation and shaping are in view, the verse addresses all people because Adam represents humanity and holds the human species’ defining traits in embryo.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r5.anchor: esas itibariyle Âdem’in yaratılması ve şekil kazanmasından bahsedilmekle birlikte, Allah onu, soyundan gelecek insanların genel bir örneği kıldığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r6.claim: God ordered the angels to prostrate to Adam to show the honor and dignity of Adam and the human species; the commentary refers readers to 2:34 for the prostration’s nature.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r6.anchor: Yüce Allah, Âdem ve onun temsil ettiği insan türünün şan ve şerefini göstermek üzere meleklere Âdem’e secde etmelerini buyurmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r7.claim: Since the passage warns unbelievers and polytheists, it reminds them that failing to know God, associating partners with Him, or disobeying Him after His honoring humanity is profound ingratitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r7.anchor: Allah’ın böylesine seçkin kılıp ikramda bulunduğu insanlardan bir kısmının O’nu tanımamaları, O’na ortak koşmaları ve buyruğuna karşı gelmelerinin ne büyük bir nankörlük

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r8.speaker: Bazı yorumcular
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r8.claim: Some identify the prostrating angels as angels of the earth, on the reasoning that angels of the heavens prostrate only to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r8.anchor: Secde eden meleklerin “yer melekleri” olduğu, çünkü “gök melekleri”nin sadece Allah’a secde ettikleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r9.speaker: Süleyman Ateş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r9.claim: Ateş proposes that the angels who prostrated were forces of nature.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r9.anchor: bunların tabiat kuvvetleri olduğu (Ateş, III, 323) yolunda görüşler ileri sürülmüşse de

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r10.claim: Because the matter belongs to the unseen and there is no sound transmitted proof, the author advises against decisive claims about which angels prostrated.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r10.anchor: konu gayb âlemiyle ilgili olduğundan elde sağlam naklî delil bulunmadıkça belirleyici yorumlardan kaçınmak uygun olur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r11.speaker: İblîs’in daha önce melekler arasında yer aldığı sonucunu çıkaranlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r11.claim: Some infer from Iblis being excepted from the prostrating angels that he had previously belonged among the angels.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r11.anchor: Âyette, secde eden meleklerden İblîs’in istisna edilmesinden, onun daha önce melekler arasında yer aldığı sonucunu çıkaranlar olmuşsa da

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r12.claim: The author rejects that inference: 18:50 calls Iblis one of the jinn, and 66:6 says angels do not disobey; unlike angels, Iblis could follow desire, and rebelled when first ordered to do something against his inclination.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:11/r12.anchor: Kehf sûresinde (18/50) onun vaktiyle cinlerden olduğu, Tahrîm sûresinde (66/6) ise meleklerin Allah’ın buyruklarına isyan etmeyecekleri bildirilmektedir.

BAQILLANI:v1p30/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r1.claim: The doctrine of ṣarfa fails: if opponents were merely diverted from imitation, comparable pre-Islamic eloquence should exist among people who were never challenged or constrained.
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r1.anchor: فلما لم يوجد في كلام من قبله مثله علم أن ما ادعاه القائل بالصرفة ظاهر البطلان

BAQILLANI:v1p30/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r2.claim: Experts in eloquence recognize when speech can be matched; someone truly at the summit of eloquence would not presume to rival the Qurʾān.
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r2.anchor: ومن كان متناهيا في فصاحته لم يجز أن يطمع في مثل هذا القرآن بحال

BAQILLANI:v1p30/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r3.claim: Claims by individuals that human speech can rival or exceed the Qurʾān do not settle the question; judgment belongs to eloquent people collectively.
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r3.anchor: والمرجوع في هذا إلى جملة الفصحاء دون الآحاد

BAQILLANI:v1p30/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r4.claim: The opponents’ claim that the Qurʾān is human speech echoes the man who thought and plotted before calling it sorcery and human words.
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r4.anchor: إنه فكر وقدر فقتل كيف قدر ثم قتل كيف قدر ثم نظر ثم عبس وبسر

BAQILLANI:v1p30/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r5.claim: If imitation were possible but prevented only by divine diversion, the miracle would lie in the prevention rather than in any excellence intrinsic to the Qurʾānic discourse.
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r5.anchor: ومما يبطل ما ذكروه من القول بالصرفة أنه لو كانت المعرضة ممكنة

BAQILLANI:v1p30/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r6.speaker: فريق منهم
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r6.claim: Another faction says everyone could produce a counterpart if they learned the special method of arrangement; the author presents this as another claim that fails to explain the Qurʾān’s distinction.
BAQILLANI:v1p30/r6.anchor: أن الكل قادرون على الإتيان بمثله وإنما يتأخرون عنه لعدم العلم بوجه ترتيب

BAQILLANI:v1p185/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p185/r1.speaker: رسول الله
BAQILLANI:v1p185/r1.claim: Abu Umāma transmits the Prophet's statement that reciting one third, one half, or all of the Quran grants a corresponding share of prophethood, without revelation.
BAQILLANI:v1p185/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله من قرأ ثلث القرآن أعطي ثلث النبوة ومن قرأ نصف القرآن أعطي نصف النبوة ومن قرأ القرآن كله أعطي النبوة كلها

BAQILLANI:v1p252/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p252/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p252/r1.claim: The Quran is miraculous in itself; the idea that it only becomes a sign after a challenge wrongly makes Moses' and Jesus' signs dependent on challenge too.
BAQILLANI:v1p252/r1.anchor: فأما من قدر أن القرآن لا يصير معجزا إلا بالتحدي إليه فهو كتقدير من ظن أن جميع آيات موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام ليست بآيات حتى التحدي إليها

BAQILLANI:v1p252/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p252/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p252/r2.claim: Challenge and the Arabs' failure reveal the Quran's existing inimitability; a non-Arab learner needs transmitted evidence of that failure, subject to reliable transmission conditions.
BAQILLANI:v1p252/r2.anchor: بل هو معجز في نفسه وإنما طريق معرفة هذا وقوفهم على العلم بعجزهم عنه

BURHAN:v4p268/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p268/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p268/r1.claim: Thumma can mark temporal delay or a non-temporal progression in qualities, highlighting the importance of what follows and prompting reflection rather than ordering events in time.
BURHAN:v4p268/r1.anchor: والحاصل انها للتراخي في الزمان وهو المعبر عنه بالمهلة وتكون للتباين في الصفات وغيرها من غير قصد مهلة زمانية

BURHAN:v4p268/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p268/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
BURHAN:v4p268/r4.claim: Because the angels were ordered to bow before humans were created, one explanation treats the sequence as saying that God formed humanity and then commanded the angels.
BURHAN:v4p268/r4.anchor: وقد أمر الله الملائكة بالسجود قبل خلقنا فالمعنى وصورناكم

BURHAN:v4p268/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p268/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
BURHAN:v4p268/r5.claim: Another explanation keeps temporal order: God began humanity's creation with Adam from clay and later formed him, and began each person's creation from a drop before forming him.
BURHAN:v4p268/r5.anchor: وقيل على بابها والمعنى ابتدأنا خلقكم لان الله تعالى خلق آدم من تراب ثم صوره وابتدأ خلق الانسان من نطفة ثم صوره

SULAMI:v1p221/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p221/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p221/r1.claim: One Sufi reading assigns each created form a mode of life: hearts live by witnessing, selves by existence, servants by their worshipped Lord, the elect by sincerity, the afterlife by knowledge, and worldly life by ignorance, construction, and delusion.
SULAMI:v1p221/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : أبدع الله الهياكل وأظهرها على أخلاق شتى وصور مختلفة

SULAMI:v1p221/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p221/r2.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v1p221/r2.claim: Abu Hafs says God's command to prostrate before Adam showed that He needs no worship: creation's worship adds nothing to His kingdom, for He is mighty before creation, after its destruction, and at resurrection.
SULAMI:v1p221/r2.anchor: قال أبو حفص : عرف الملائكة استغناءه عن عبادتهم

SULAMI:v1p221/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p221/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p221/r3.claim: One view distinguishes God's command to prostrate as an obligation from the command to leave as humiliation; the angels' prostration honored Adam and obeyed God.
SULAMI:v1p221/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : قوله لإبليس أمر تكليف وقوله

ITQAN:v1p216/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p216/r1.speaker: القراب
ITQAN:v1p216/r1.claim: Al-Qurab says restricting recitation to the seven has no Prophetic precedent; a later collection spread the limit, though no one had endorsed it.
ITQAN:v1p216/r1.anchor: وقال القراب في الشافي التمسك بقراءة سبعة من القراء دون غيرهم ليس فيه أثر ولا سنة وإنما هو من جمع بعض المتأخرين

ITQAN:v1p216/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p216/r2.speaker: الكواشي
ITQAN:v1p216/r2.claim: Al-Kawashi defines an accepted reading as one with a sound chain, valid Arabic, and agreement with the official consonantal text; missing any condition makes it irregular.
ITQAN:v1p216/r2.anchor: وقال الكواشي كل ما صح سنده واستقام وجهه في العربية ووافق خط المصحف الإمام فهو من السبعة المنصوصة ومتى فقد شرط من الثلاثة فهو الشاذ

ITQAN:v1p216/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p216/r3.speaker: تقي الدين السبكي
ITQAN:v1p216/r3.claim: Al-Subki rejects restricting accepted readings to seven: Yaqub and Abu Ja'far were accepted alongside them, and famous readings known to specialists remain permissible when they fit the text's script.
ITQAN:v1p216/r3.anchor: فقال في شرح المنهاج قال الأصحاب تجوز القراءة في الصلاة وغيرها بالقراءات السبع ولا تجوز بالشاذة وظاهر هذا يوهم أن غير السبع المشهورة من الشواذ

ITQAN:v1p216/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p216/r4.speaker: ولد السبكي
ITQAN:v1p216/r4.claim: The younger al-Subki says seven readings are unanimously mutawatir, while denying that the other three are mutawatir is untenable; his father permitted teaching all ten.
ITQAN:v1p216/r4.anchor: وقال ولده في منع الموانع إنما قلنا في جمع الجوامع والسبع متواترة ثم قلنا في الشاذ والصحيح إنه ما وراء العشرة

ITQAN:v1p279/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p279/r1.speaker: النووي
ITQAN:v1p279/r1.claim: Al-Nawawi says the amount recited should fit the reader: those pursuing subtle understanding or public duties should read enough to preserve them; others may read more without fatigue or rushed recitation.
ITQAN:v1p279/r1.anchor: وقال النووي في الأذكار المختار أن ذلك يختلف باختلاف الأشخاص فمن كان يظهر له بدقيق الفكر لطائف ومعارف فليقتصر على قدر يحصل له معه كمال فهم ما يقرأ

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r1.claim: Scattering defeated people in battle is called scattering by metaphor: small objects are the literal objects scattered, while the transferred use preserves the general sense of disorderly dispersal.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r1.anchor: استعارة لأن النثر في الأصل للأجسام الصغار كالدراهم والدنانير والجواهر والحبوب ونحوها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r2.claim: Skewering two mounted men is called stringing or composing by analogy with threading small bodies; if such grouping of large bodies were common, the word would be literal for them too.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r2.anchor: ثم لما حصل في الشخصين من الرجال أن يجمعهما الحاذق المبدع في الطعن في رمح واحد ذلك الضرب من الجمع عبر عنه بالنظم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r3.claim: Applying tearing to rock is metaphorical but close to literal because rock can crack; tearing, splitting, and cracking share the sense of separation, unlike a figurative breach of modesty with no physical split.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r3.anchor: الشق والصدع حقيقة في الصفاة ونعلم أن الخرق يجامعها في الجنس لأن الكل تفريق وقطع

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r4.claim: Calling a breach of decorum خرق is outside this near-literal metaphorical class, since no actual splitting is involved.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p42/r4.anchor: لو قلت خرق الحشمة لم يكن من الحقيقة في شىء وكان خارجا من هذا الفن

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r1.claim: Conjunctive لا introduces a new negation; it cannot be used to carve out an item already included in a general negation, for which و لا is required.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r1.anchor: وهي موضوعة لأن تنفي بها ما بدأت ، فأوجبته لا لأن تفيد بها النفي في شيء قد نفيته

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r2.claim: After ما جاءني إلا زيد, the wording has already explicitly negated arrival by everyone else, so adding لا عمرو repeats a negation already made.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r2.anchor: فقد نفيت أن يكون قد جاءك أحد غيره

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r3.claim: إنما جاءني زيد and زيد هو الجائي assert a particular arrival positively; excluding others follows by implication, not an expressed negation, so لا عمرو may follow.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p264/r3.anchor: وهو كلام كما تراه مثبت ليس فيه نفي البتة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265#2/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265#2/r1.claim: The usual order is to put the object before إلا: ما ضرب زيدا إلا عمرو, restricting the agent to striking Zayd.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265#2/r1.anchor: وإنما الأكثر أن تقدم المفعول على ' إلا ' ، نحو : ما ضرب زيدا إلا عمر و

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265#2/r2.speaker: هم
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265#2/r2.claim: Some analyze ما ضرب إلا عمرو زيدا as two clauses, with زيدا governed by an omitted verb after the initial statement.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265#2/r2.anchor: وأن زيدا منصوب بفعل مضمر ، حتى كأن المتكلم بذلك أبهم في أول أمره

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265#2/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265#2/r3.claim: To restrict عمرو specifically to striking Zayd, the speaker must state the object first; without it, listeners infer that only عمرو struck at all and that every victim was struck by him.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r1.claim: Words signify meanings and can disclose them as they are; a sign cannot itself transform the meaning or give it a quality it did not have.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r1.anchor: الألفاظ أدلة على المعاني ، وليس للدليل إلا أن يعلمك الشيء على ما يكون عليه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r2.speaker: العلماء
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r2.claim: The familiar rule says that whoever takes a bare meaning and clothes it in wording of his own becomes more entitled to it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r2.anchor: قول العلماء حيث ذكروا الأخذ والسرقة : إن من أخذ معنى عاريا فكساه لفظا من عنده كان أحق به

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r3.claim: Jurjani challenges the rule: a meaning cannot be bare of words, and if the borrower adds no quality or merit, new wording alone cannot make it his.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r3.anchor: من أين يتصور أن يكون هاهنا معنى عار من لفظ يدل عليه ؟

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r4.claim: Clothing a meaning must mean giving it a new form; treating metaphor as merely substituting a word cannot explain added merit or a stronger claim to the meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r4.anchor: والاستعارة عندكم مقصورة على مجرد اللفظ ، ولا ترون المستعير يصنع بالمعنى شيئا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r5.claim: As an example of reworking an existing meaning, Jurjani introduces Abu Tammam's verse based on a line by Abu Nukhayla.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p346/r5.anchor: فإن من أحسن شيء فيه ما صنع أبو تمام في بيت أبي نخيلة

AKHFASH:v1p321/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p321/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p321/r1.claim: Thumma may mean waw here; alternatively the plural address is directed to Adam, as when a group is told they were struck though only their chief was struck.
AKHFASH:v1p321/r1.anchor: وقال {ثم صورناكم ثم قلنا للملائكة} لأن "ثم" في معنى الواو

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p97/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p97/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p97/r8.claim: The plural creation and shaping address refers to Adam, since humanity descended from him.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p97/r8.anchor: أراد: خلقنا آدم وصورناه، فجعل الخلق لهم، إذ كانوا منه.

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r1.claim: One view gives both occurrences of ثم no chronological force, treating them like واو because creation and formation followed the command to the angels.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r1.anchor: فمنهم من لم يلتزم فيها ترتيبا وجعلها بمنزلة الواو

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r2.claim: Another view takes both ثم as ordering events in the account rather than in time; the author says this explanation adds little.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r2.anchor: ومنهم من قال: هي للترتيب لا في الزمان بل للترتيب في الإخبار، ولا طائل في هذا

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r3.claim: A third view gives both occurrences their original temporal ordering sense.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r3.anchor: ومنهم من قال: هي للترتيب الزماني وهذا هو موضوعها الأصلي

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r4.claim: A fourth view reads the first ثم temporally and the second as ordering the report rather than events.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r4.anchor: ومنهم من قال: الأولى للترتيب الزماني والثانية للترتيب الإخباري

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r5.claim: To preserve temporal order in both clauses, some supply two omitted nouns: God created and formed your forefathers, meaning Adam.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r5.anchor: والتقدير: ولقد خلقنا آباءكم ثم صورنا آباءكم ثم قلنا

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r6.claim: Others take Adam himself as the plural addressee, using the plural for honor and because he is the source of all people.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r6.anchor: بصيغة الجمع وهو واحد تعظيما له ولأنه أصل الجميع

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r7.claim: Another explanation addresses Adam's descendants while intending their ancestor, a common Arabic usage illustrated by the rescue from Pharaoh.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r7.anchor: وهذا من باب الخطاب لشخص والمراد به غيره كقوله: { وإذ نجيناكم من آل فرعون }

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r8.claim: A line about Tamim's victory at Dhi Qar illustrates addressing descendants about an event performed by their forebears.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r8.anchor:
وأنشدوا على ذلك قوله:
2144 إذا افتخرت يوما تميم بقوسها

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r9.claim: Among those who make only the second ثم informational, one view addresses Adam in the first clause and his descendants in the second.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r9.anchor: المراد بالخطاب الأول آدم وبالثاني ذريته

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r10.claim: Other explanations place creation in Adam's loins and formation in mothers' wombs, or creation of spouses followed by formation of bodies.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r10.anchor: ولقد خلقناكم في ظهر آدم ثم صورناكم في بطون أمهاتكم

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r11.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r11.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la transmits the unusual interpretation that God created your spouses and then formed your bodies.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r11.anchor: وهذا غريب نقله القاضي أبو يعلى في " المعتمد "

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r12.claim: Another view says people were created as drops in men's loins then formed in women's wombs.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r12.anchor: خلقناكم نطفا في أصلاب الرجال ثم صورناكم في أرحام النساء

SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r13.claim: Another view places creation and formation in mothers' wombs, with formation afterward by making hearing and sight.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11/r13.anchor: ولقد خلقناكم في بطون أمهاتكم وصورناكم فيها بعد الخلق بشق السمع والبصر

SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r1.claim: The author notes that his discussion of the exception of Iblis has already appeared in the commentary on al-Baqara.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: { إلا إبليس } تقدم الكلام عليه في البقرة.

SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r2.claim: لم يكن is an independent clause answering an implied question; the pause falls after إبليس, as with أبى in al-Baqara.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r2.anchor: لأنها جواب سؤال مقدر، وهذا كما تقدم في قوله في البقرة

SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r3.claim: Another explanation says the clause emphatically restates that the exception was excluded from the prostrators' negation.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: فائدة هذه الجملة التوكيد لما أخرجه الاستثناء من نفي سجود إبليس

SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa parses لم يكن من الساجدين as a circumstantial clause: Iblis was in a state of refusing to prostrate.
SAMIN-DURR:7:11#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " إنها في محل نصب على الحال أي: إلا إبليس حال كونه ممتنعا من السجود "

ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r1.speaker: الأخفش
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash says the hamza in مصائب replaces a weakened wāw in مصيبة; al-Zajjaj rejects this as a poor, unnecessary analogy.
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r1.anchor: وزعم الأخفش أن مصائب إنما وقعت الهمزة فيها بدلا من الواو

ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r2.speaker: الأخفش
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash treats ثم as meaning و, but al-Zajjaj rejects this: ثم always marks what follows what was mentioned.
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r2.anchor: زعم الأخفش أن (ثم) ههنا في معنى الواو، وهذا خطأ لا يجيزه الخليل

ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r3.claim: The address recounts the origin of Adam's creation: God began him as soil, then shaped him; the source cites Adam's creation from dust as evidence.
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r3.anchor: فإنما المعنى إنا بدأنا خلق آدم ثم صورناه، فابتداء خلق آدم التراب

ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r4.claim: Eve was created from one of Adam's ribs, and shaping followed; Adam's descendants were then created from seed and formed, so ثم retains its sequential sense.
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r4.anchor: وبدأ خلق حواء من ضلع من أضلاعه، ثم وقعت الصورة بعد ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r5.claim: God commanded the angels to prostrate only after finishing Adam's creation.
ZAJJAJ:v2p321/r5.anchor: أي بعد الفراغ من خلق آدم أمرت الملائكة بالسجود.

ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r1.claim: Iblis is an exception from those commanded to prostrate, not an exception from the angels; the next verse confirms he was commanded.
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r1.anchor: استثناء ليس من الأول، ولكنه ممن أمر بالسجود.

ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n9/r1.claim: The sequence describes gradual human development, both from embryo to full individual existence and across the evolution of the human race.
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n9/r1.anchor: is meant to bring out the fact of man's gradual development, in the individual sense, from the embryonic stage to full-fledged existence

ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r1.claim: Asad treats God's command that the angels prostrate before Adam as allegorical and points to 2:30–34 and its notes.
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r1.anchor: As regards God's allegorical command to the angels to "prostrate themselves" before Adam, see 2:30-34

ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r2.claim: Because the passage first addresses all mankind, Adam's name here symbolizes the whole human race.
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r2.anchor: his name symbolizes, in this context, the whole human race

ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r3.speaker: Western scholars
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r3.claim: Western scholars commonly regard Iblis as a corruption of the Greek diabolos, from which English “devil” derives.
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r3.anchor: Western scholars usually take it for granted that the name "Iblis" is a corruption of the Greek word diabolos

ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r4.claim: Asad rejects the Greek-borrowing claim: there is no evidence that pre-Islamic Arabs borrowed such terms from Greeks, while Greek mythology drew substantially on earlier South Arabian civilization.
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r4.anchor: There is, however, not the slightest evidence that the pre-Islamic Arabs borrowed this or any other mythological term from the Greeks

ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r5.claim: Asad proposes that Greek diabolos Hellenized Arabic Iblis, derived from ablasa (“despaired,” “gave up hope,” or “became broken in spirit”); Greek familiarity could explain the association despite the word’s Greek origin.
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r5.anchor: One may, therefore, assume with something approaching certainty that the Greek diabolos is a Hellenized form of the Arabic name for the Fallen Angel

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p112/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p112/r1.speaker: author
